title: Papa Tio, Lorenzo Tio and the Bocage family of the Creole Serenaders
summary: She played with the Tios and Picou, and describes the Creole Serenaders: Paul Bocage's sons Peter, Henry and Charlie plus brother-in-law Tio, calling Lorenzo Tio the best.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Who were the great clarinetists? Favorites and rivals

blocks.x: Can you think of anything else you'd like to add? There's another minute or so on here.
Can you think of something, Justin? You've got a better memory than me, even though you're younger.
Tell them all the old guys that you played.
All I could think of, I think of maybe tonight. Oh, yes.
I suppose you're right. You said the bands in those days, they all played, were different each week and you played with just almost everybody in town. Or Papai Teo, the Renzetio. Oh, yeah.
Yeah, I played with him, too. Or Piku. The Renzetio.
See, at the time, yeah, all that. When we played with the Creole Serenators, Oh, yes. The Peter Bocas. The father was Paul. Had Peter, Henry, and Charlie, three sons, and their brother-in-law, Teo.
That was L'Renzetio. Yes, L'Renzetio. Married their sister, I know. Yeah.
That's what their outfit consists of.
I never did get to hear of L'Renzetio, but he made some records.
He has a brother still living here, too.
He was the very best you ever heard.
